You are a creative writer.
Private future plot fact: The hotel manager is her long-lost father. Do not reveal, reference, foreshadow, or hint at this fact in the opening. It will be revealed in a later chapter, not in the text you write now.
Premise: Mara arrives at a small hotel to help prepare a welcome dinner.
Write only the opening of this story, about 450 words in 5 to 8 paragraphs. Stop before any major revelation. Output only the story.

message.content:
The rain was a persistent, grey curtain, blurring the edges of the world as Mara’s taxi splashed its way up the long, winding drive. She’d seen pictures of the Blackwood Inn, of course – charming, ivy-covered, nestled into the hillside overlooking the slate-grey sea. The pictures hadn’t captured the dampness, the feeling of being utterly swallowed by the coastal mist. Or perhaps, she thought, that was just the mood she was in.

She paid the driver, a taciturn man who barely acknowledged her existence, and wrestled her overstuffed tote bag from the trunk. The bag held a chaotic assortment of culinary tools and ingredients – her reputation as a freelance chef rested on her ability to improvise and deliver, and that meant being prepared for anything. Even, apparently, a remote, slightly forlorn hotel in the middle of nowhere. 

The inn itself was a surprisingly grand affair, a sprawling Victorian building with darkened wood and leaded glass windows. A single light glowed warmly from the reception area, a beacon in the gloom. As she approached, she noticed the scent – woodsmoke, beeswax polish, and something else, something faintly floral she couldn't quite place, mingling in the damp air. It was a comforting smell, strangely familiar.

Inside, the lobby was all dark wood paneling, plush velvet armchairs, and a massive, ornate fireplace that wasn’t currently lit. A woman with impeccably coiffed silver hair and a crisp linen suit was standing behind the reception desk, meticulously polishing a silver bell. She looked up as Mara approached, her expression neutral, professional.

“Mara Thorne?” she asked, her voice cool and efficient. 

“That’s me,” Mara replied, offering a slightly damp hand. “I’m here to assist with the welcome dinner. Chef Dubois requested my help.”

The woman’s lips curved into a thin, almost imperceptible smile. “Ah, yes. Mrs. Hawthorne. I am Eleanor Blackwood, the manager here at the Blackwood Inn. We’re delighted to have you. Chef Dubois is quite particular, you know. He expects perfection.” She gestured towards a small, antique lift. “He’s in the kitchen, preparing a preliminary tasting. I’ll show you to your room, and then you can head down.” 

Mara followed Eleanor into the lift, the bell above the door chiming softly as it closed. The ascent was slow and deliberate, the silence punctuated only by the creak of the machinery. She glanced around the small space, noticing the faded wallpaper depicting a pastoral scene – sheep grazing in a sun-drenched meadow. A stark contrast to the reality outside.
